item.headline: Investor frenzy for SpaceX IPO may overwhelm concerns about losses and governance
causal_chain: SpaceX IPO frenzy signals strong retail and institutional appetite for private space/defense-adjacent names
Pre-IPO enthusiasm compresses risk premia on adjacent listed space and aerospace names temporarily, as capital rotates toward the narrative
Governance and loss concerns are noted but historically subordinated to growth narratives at this stage — IPO pricing risk is forward-looking and does not yet have a clearing price to anchor
item.directional_bias: thematic/narrative; no clean directional trade on listed names

sizing_recommendation.rationale: SpaceX is private; no direct portfolio exposure. Adjacent listed names have weak causal links. Signal is forward-looking and speculative; no actionable listed ticker.

item.reasoning: This is a thematic/narrative item about pre-IPO sentiment. SpaceX is not listed, no portfolio name is directly affected, and the causal chain from 'IPO frenzy' to a listed ticker's price is weak and indirect. The governance/losses caveat further reduces conviction. Classified as watch-level (score 4) because IPO momentum stories occasionally foreshadow sector re-ratings, but no action is warranted here.

item.headline: Xi's clash with Trump over Japan signals rising Asia security tensions
causal_chain: US-China friction over Japan's security posture elevates Taiwan Strait / East China Sea risk premium
Elevated Asia security tensions increase probability of export-control escalation and supply-chain disruption targeting semiconductor and tech hardware flows
Risk-off rotation out of Asia-exposed equities; ex-US equity indices (ACWX, EWJ) reprice downward; Taiwan foundry equities face geopolitical discount widening
item.directional_bias: bearish Asia-exposed equities, risk-off tilt for ex-US tech supply chain

sizing_recommendation.rationale: Layer 0 signal only, sourced from a single Seeking Alpha summary with no body text — insufficient specificity to initiate; no portfolio positions directly threatened at actionable magnitude

item.reasoning: The headline signals US-China friction over Japan but carries no body text, no named policy action, and no confirmed event — it is a characterization of a diplomatic signal rather than a discrete catalyst. The causal chain to markets is plausible (Asia security risk → tech supply-chain discount → ex-US equity de-rating) but requires at minimum a named policy move (sanctions, military posture change, export restriction) before the signal clears noise. ACWX and TSM are on the radar or broadly affected; MSFT carries secondary Asia supply-chain exposure but the link is too attenuated to change stance on a held position. Stand down until a harder catalyst is reported.
